inputs.root_cause: After XLIFF's 8 consecutive productive ticks exhausted its easily-reachable clusters, surveyed UBL's remaining 30 unresolved obligations (untouched since event 223) and found a fresh, genuine 6-obligation cluster about element-order validation, entirely unbuilt: neither the model nor validate() checked child-element sequence order against the schema at all.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-UBL-OBL-3B43504E9C74003C and 5 cross-capability duplicates (26CD31E7F8CF91E1, 31DE92275AF5F6EF, 4936871F9800219B, 71FF376D05E7219A, CDADC5CFB25A9B9E) -- all promoted missing->partial
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 9 new tests prove validate() now detects out-of-order children among the same 13 already-modeled complexTypes the cardinality cluster covers, including a case that directly proves a caught schema-order transcription risk (cac:LegalMonetaryTotal's PayableAmount) is handled correctly.
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed ubl's remaining 30 unresolved obligations (13 missing, 17 partial) and found a 6-obligation cluster sharing identical rule_text about element order, confirmed via substring search against the obligation register (the initial exact-string match missed one member, SAL-UBL-OBL-26CD31E7F8CF91E1 under UBL-SIGN-001, whose own missing_behavior text used slightly different phrasing -- caught by re-searching with a substring match on the rule_text itself rather than trusting the missing_behavior summary text).

2. Extracted the FULL, ordered child-element sequence for all 13 already-modeled complexTypes (PartyType, AddressType, ContactType, PaymentMeansType, FinancialAccountType, CreditNoteLineType, ResponseType, DocumentReferenceType, InvoiceLineType, TaxSubtotalType, TaxTotalType, MonetaryTotalType, ExternalReferenceType) directly from the pinned OASIS UBL 2.3 CommonAggregateComponents schema, in one pass.

3. Programmatically filtered each complexType's full sequence down to only the already-modeled single-occurrence fields from the existing cardinality-check frozensets, preserving true schema order, with an assertion that the filtered field set exactly matches the expected field set for every component. This caught a genuine transcription risk directly: cac:LegalMonetaryTotal's underlying MonetaryTotalType declares cbc:PayableAmount LAST in its sequence (after ChargeTotalAmount), not second (after LineExtensionAmount) as a hand-transcription based on the existing frozenset's insertion order would have incorrectly produced.

4. Added _ORDER_CHECKED_COMPONENTS (a qname-keyed dispatch dict, mirroring _CARDINALITY_CHECKED_COMPONENTS exactly), _order_violations(), and _order_diagnostics() to validator.py: for each checked component, walks its children in document order, tracks a running high-water-mark index among only the checked fields present, and flags any checked field whose expected index is lower than the high-water mark (proving it appeared out of declared order). Deliberately does not re-check cardinality -- a genuine duplicate simply compares equal against the high-water mark and does not spuriously trigger a false order violation.
5. Wired the new function into validate() alongside the existing cardinality check.

6. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: Party with PostalAddress before Contact validates cleanly, the reverse is a violation; LegalMonetaryTotal with PayableAmount correctly last validates cleanly, PayableAmount before TaxExclusiveAmount is a violation (directly proving the caught transcription risk is now handled correctly); fields not yet modeled as checkable may legitimately intersperse among checked fields without a false violation -- all 5 cases correct on the first attempt.

7. Ran the full pre-existing ubl suite (928 tests, zero new fixtures) against the new check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 928 passed unchanged, confirming zero pre-existing fixture used any of these 13 components in schema-violating order.
8. Wrote 9 formal tests, all passing on the first attempt.

9. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (937 passed, was 928, +9), and the full 6-format regression (3367 passed, was 3358, +9; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

10. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-f7a9100545d2f15b, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

11. Promoted all 6 obligations to partial (not implemented): full element-order validation across every UBL complexType remains a genuinely large, separate undertaking (only these 13 already-modeled complexTypes are covered), and UBL-WRITE-001's companion 'write elements in schema-valid order' obligation remains separately unbuilt -- this slice only detects existing out-of-order documents, it does not make the writer reorder elements automatically. Matches the honest scope discipline the cardinality cluster itself has maintained across all 5 of its own ticks this session.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ubl/ -q -- 937 passed, was 928 passed (928 passed unchanged BEFORE writing new tests, confirming zero false positives)

.venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3367 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3358 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule; every declared order read directly from the pinned schema, filtered programmatically, not transcribed by hand.
